description: snappyHexMesh cannot currently produce a mesh usable with cyclic BCs. Evidence (verified 2026-08-13): snappy_hex_mesh/snapping.rs collects ONLY PatchKind::Wall patch points to project, and its module header states the parallel/COUPLED-PATCH and displacement-diffusion machinery is deliberately omitted; grep finds zero 'cyclic' mentions anywhere under outram-foam-mesh/src/snappy_hex_mesh/. blockMesh DOES parse cyclic/cyclicAMI into PatchKind::Cyclic (block_mesh.rs:1664), so a cyclic background mesh can be built — but castellation+snapping do not preserve face-for-face conformity across a coupled patch PAIR, so the N/S and E/W patches stop matching and the cyclic BC is invalid. Needed: (a) treat coupled patch pairs as constrained during castellation (refine both sides identically), (b) constrain snapping displacement on cyclic patch points to the patch plane / apply the transform to the partner, (c) a conformity assertion (same face count + matching face centres under the cyclic transform) as the V&V gate. Raised by external GitHub issue #3 (subchannel with spacer grid + fuel rods, needs cyclic N/S and E/W). Distinct from op-ulo.5, which is the SOLVER-side cyclic support in outram-foam-basic-lib.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Done in commit 47476d1308. Two gaps fixed: (1) castellation now emits Cyclic patch pairs via CastellationControls::with_cyclic_axis, with halves sorted into corresponding order so local face i <-> face i holds by construction; (2) snapping no longer freezes cyclic-plane points — displacement is projected into the plane then partner-averaged across the seam. New snappy_hex_mesh::cyclic module provides check_conformity, the geometric V&V gate FvMeshBuilder lacks. Measured: seam motion 2.474460e-2 m with conformity preserved to 1e-9 m, vs exactly 0 m frozen baseline; 76-face pair, max non-ortho 25.44 deg, 0 inverted cells. Translational only — rotational/AMI rejected. NOTE: still does NOT close GitHub issue #3 — that needs STEP->STL import (absent) and a two-phase solver (outram-foam-multiphase is scaffold), and the reporter's geometry.zip could not be fetched.

title: outram-foam-mesh: snappyHexMesh must preserve cyclic (coupled) patch conformity — blocks cyclic BC meshes

description:
The ssnv101a harness (crates/outram-park-fork-offbeat/tests/astest_ssnv101a.rs) does PURE STRESS CONTROL with constant material properties. Every remaining astest candidate needs more than that, so the next unit of work is extending the harness, not attempting another deck with the current one.

TWO CAPABILITIES NEEDED:

1. MIXED strain/stress control. ssnv126a is displacement-controlled: N5-N8 carry DZ=0.1 over a 30-long specimen (eps_zz = 3.3333e-3) while the lateral faces are traction-free, so the constraint set is 'eps_zz prescribed, sigma_xx = sigma_yy = sigma_xy = sigma_xz = sigma_yz = 0'. The existing fixed point solves for all six strain components against six prescribed stresses; it needs to accept a per-component mask choosing strain-prescribed or stress-prescribed.

2. Temperature-dependent material properties, evaluated per step. ssnv126a is anisothermal: T = 1000 K constant to t=2e5, then ramping to 1025 K at t=2e6. The run stops at NUME_INST_FIN=60, which is t=1.6e6, where T interpolates to about 1019.4 K — so temperature genuinely varies over the analysed range.

MATERIAL FUNCTIONS IN ssnv126a, all piecewise-linear in TEMP with CONSTANT extrapolation both sides:
  N_T  (900, 12.2)      (1000, 10.8)      (1025, 10.45)
  M_T  (900, 1/10.5)    (1000, 1/9.8)     (1025, 1/9.625)
  K_T  (900, 1/2110)    (1000, 1/1450)    (1025, 1/1285)
  A_T  (900, 3191.62)   (1000, 2511.35)   (1025, 2341.3)
  R_T  (900, 6.3)       (1000, 5.2)       (1025, 4.925)
Plus KD_T, a DEFI_NAPPE — a 2-D table over (TEMP, X) with TEMP in (900, 1000, 1025, 1050) and each row a piecewise-linear function of X with LINEAIRE extrapolation. Bilinear interpolation, not just 1-D.

ALSO NOTE: the deck sets ALGO_INTE='RUNGE_KUTTA'. The damage port deliberately follows upstream's Runge-Kutta RATE EQUATIONS with the NEWTON discretisation, because upstream's three integrators disagree with each other. So a discrepancy against VALE_CALC on this deck may be a discretisation difference rather than a formulation error, and the test doc must say which it is rather than assuming.

WHY ssnv126a IS STILL THE RIGHT TARGET once the harness exists: it is the only remaining single-element 3D case (a 3x3x30 HEXA8 prism), it carries 32 reference values — the most by a wide margin — and it exercises the damage module where two upstream defects were deliberately reproduced (nmvexi wrong material slots, nmvecd damaging elastic steps). If our value matches VALE_REFE but not VALE_CALC there, that is evidence the defect analysis was right; record it, do not 'fix' the port.

The alternatives need a change of FORMULATION rather than of driver, which is why they rank below it: ssnv172b is C_PLAN plane stress, ssnv124b is 3D_INCO_UPG incompressible mixed u/p/g over 16 elements, ssnv101b is 2D with two QUAD4 elements and re-tests a law already covered.

Inputs verified present in ssnv126a.export (comm + mail only), unlike ssnv113a.
